doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Dissertation on the percussion concerto
summary: She wrote a history and analysis of percussion concertos including Milhaud's, and composed one.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I wrote, I analyzed, it’s a history of the percussion concerto, solo percussion and orchestra. So I did a big history of that, I analyzed the concerto by Darius Milhaud, which is basically the first one for percussion and orchestra, and I wrote a concerto and analyzed that, did a performance guide, and there you have it. And I think it put me to sleep by. And somebody at NYU recently came and said, “I checked out your dissertation,” I’m like oh [yawns] enjoy it as much as I did? So it wasn’t really like having lofty goals to be a professor or anything. I just wanted — I thought it would be ridiculous not to finish it. And also it always motivates me that for teaching there and becoming friends with my doctoral committee and working with them professionally that well they’re going to really think I’m a jackass if I don’t finish this. So I didn’t want to look like a quitter, and I’m not, it’s just I work better under pressure.
